scope: Proposition 5.4 (Low-frequency barrier) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-regularity-of-stationary-integral-varifolds-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 346 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f12bd8f9ace9a350), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Along every path in Theorem 5.2, the wells can be chosen piecewise constantly, with at most Q − 1 mergers. There is a positive piecewise smooth parameter k, bounded above by a small fixed constant and satisfying between mergers ka k = q = − k a2 , (5.17) such that the comparison (5.15) holds. Here C1 is fixed and sufficiently large. Uniformly along the path, log(1/k) = o(a0) as T → ∞. Before any hypothetical first failure of the barrier, the following estimates hold, with E ≤ a−P0/2: U̇ ≤ 2s2 Ds + Cs2 Dtr + EI, (5.18) s2 Rs ≥ 4k(s2 Ds − Cs2 Dtr) − 4k2 U − EkI. (5.19) With more than one well, in addition, Ż + c2 (log a)2 a s2 Dtr ≤ a−P0 I. (5.20) The transition terms are absent with one well. By increasing the fixed exponents in the construction, E can be smaller than any prescribed inverse power of a.
